Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to Persistent Systems 
Earnings Conference call for the 2nd Quarter FY27, ended September 30, 
2026.  
 
We have with us on the call today: 
1. Dr. Anand Deshpande, Chairman and Managing Director 
2. Mr. Sandeep Kalra, Executive Director and Chief Executive Officer  
3. Mr. Vinit Teredesai, Executive Director and Chief Financial Officer 
4. Mr. Nitish Shrivastava, Chief Technology Officer, Engineering Hyper 
Productivity) 
5. Mr. Saurabh Dwivedi, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Strategy.  
 
Please note that all participants' lines will be in listen-only mode and there 
will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after management's 
opening remarks. 
 
Should you need any assistance during the conference call, please raise 
your hand from the Participant tab on the screen. While asking questions, 
please identify yourself and your company. Please note that this 
conference is being recorded. 
 
I now hand over the conference to Mr. Saurabh Dwivedi. Thank you and 
over to you, sir.  
Saurabh Dwivedi: 
Thank you, Rashi. 
 
A very good day, everyone. We sincerely appreciate your presence and 
participation in today's call.  Let me quickly outline the agenda for today's 
call. 
• Sandeep will begin with an overview of our Q2 results, commentary 
on the business and update on our acquisition of Nagarro.  
• Vinit will take you through the financial details and key operational 
metrics for Q2.  
• Nitish will provide details on expansion of our AI capabilities and 
representative AI wins in the quarter gone by. 
• I will then provide an overview of our key deal wins and awards and 
recognitions for this quarter. 
• Sandeep will then come back for a quick summary of the prepared 
remarks, post which we will open the conference for questions.

Persistent Systems Limited 
 
 
Page 3 of 25 
 
 
Let me also remind you that as part of our prepared remarks and during 
Q&A, we may make certain statements which are forward-looking and may 
involve significant uncertainty. Persistent does not take any responsibility 
to update such forward-looking statements, and your discretion is 
warranted while making any investment decisions. With this, let me hand 
over to Sandeep for his prepared remarks.  
Sandeep Kalra: 
Thank you, Saurabh. Good morning, good afternoon, good evening to all of 
you, depending on where you're joining from. I hope all of you are doing 
well. Let me start with a quick financial summary of the quarter gone by.  
We achieved a healthy revenue growth of 7.8% quarter-on-quarter and 
20% year-on-year delivering USD 487.6 million in Q2 FY27. This marks our 
26th sequential quarter of revenue growth. In rupee terms, the growth for 
the quarter came in at 8.4% quarter-on-quarter and 30.3% year-on-year. In 
constant currency terms, the growth for the quarter was 7.8% quarter-on-
quarter and 20.8% year-on-year. The EBIT margin for the quarter came in 
at 15%, translating to an EBIT growth of 1.6% quarter-on-quarter and 
19.5% year-on-year.  
The operating profit after tax for the quarter came in at 10.6%, translating 
to a PAT growth of 2.5% quarter-on-quarter and 5% year-on-year. The 
reported profit after tax for the quarter came in at 7.5%. I would like to 
point out that the reported PAT includes exceptional one-time expenses as 
part of Nagarro acquisition, resulting in approximately 3.1% impact for the 
quarter. Vinit, our CFO, will provide a detailed colour on the financials and 
margin movement later in this call.  
Coming to the order book for the quarter, the total contract value for the 
quarter stood at USD 633.5 million, with total contract value of new 
bookings coming in at USD 367.1 million. The annual contract value of 
bookings for this quarter was USD 481 million, out of which the annual 
contract value from new bookings contributed to USD 262.3 million. To 
remind everyone, both TCV and ACV numbers include all bookings, small 
and large, renewals as well as new bookings across existing and newer 
customers.  
Also, as highlighted in our earlier calls, our revenue conversion on a 
quarterly basis is a function of ACV bookings closed in previous quarters, 
as well as the conversion from multi-year deals booked in previous years, 
which are included in our total contract value or TCV bookings that we 
announce on a quarterly basis.

Persistent Systems Limited 
 
 
Page 4 of 25 
 
 
Now, let me give you some colour on our client movement across various 
reported categories. This quarter, we witnessed healthy year-on-year 
growth among our various client buckets. Our top 5 customers' revenue 
grew by 38.9%, top 10 by 29.9%, top 20 by 25%, top 50 by 24% and top 100 
by 21.6%.  
Coming to the year-on-year movement of customers across various 
reported buckets: Customers with annual revenues greater than 75 million 
remained stable at 4. Those with USD 50 million plus annual revenue 
remained stable at 4. Customers in the USD 20 million plus category 
increased from 12 to 13. Those in USD 10 million plus category increased 
from 25 to 34. Customers in USD 5 million plus category increased from 56 
to 60 and the customers in USD 1 million plus category increased from 191 
to 280. This healthy movement of customers across various revenue 
brackets demonstrates our team's consistent ability in cultivating deeper, 
more resilient partnerships with customers over time. 
Now, coming to the details of our performance across various 
geographies. In terms of year-on-year growth this quarter in USD terms, 
North America revenue grew by 22.5%. Revenue in Europe declined 8.5% 
largely because of two client-specific events. One of our key clients in the 
European region was acquired by a larger strategic last year, which led to 
the ramp-down of our program with them over the last several quarters. 
Another engagement completed its planned ramp-down as a part of a 
fixed-price engagement. Both are one-off, client-specific events rather 
than a sign of broader geographic demand trends. Revenue in India grew 
by 19.4% and the rest of the world grew by 67% although on a smaller base.  
Coming to industry segments growth on a year-on-year basis. This 
quarter's growth was led by Software, High-Tech and Emerging verticals 
coming in at 28.5% followed by Banking, Financial Services and Insurance 
at 16.2% and Healthcare and Lifesciences vertical at 12% respectively on a 
year-on-year basis. Growth in our Software, High-Tech and Emerging 
Industries vertical was driven by our new software reinvention offering 
launched during the quarter underpinned by the theme of the large deal 
that we announced last quarter. 
As you know, high-tech is an industry that is most affected by advances in 
AI. Enterprise software companies as well as enterprises are rethinking 
how software is built and maintained. Our Software Reinvention offering is 
designed to help software and technology companies deliver AI native

Persistent Systems Limited 
 
 
Page 5 of 25 
 
products as well as modernize their legacy products for an AI first world. 
This is traditionally a segment where Persistent has always been 
significantly ahead of our peers, and we are confident that this offering will 
drive growth across the business creating a significant mode for us over the 
next several years. My colleague Nitish will cover it in more detail on this 
offering in the AI updates section a little later in this call.  
Let me now provide you with an update on the agreement to acquire 
Nagarro that we announced earlier in June this year. As you may be aware, 
we signed a business combination agreement in late June time frame with 
Nagarro, a leading European digital engineering firm aimed at creating an 
AI-led global engineering powerhouse serving clients with end-to-end 
capabilities with over $2.9 billion in revenue run rate and 46,000 plus 
professionals across 40 countries. To refresh everyone on the acquisition 
rationale, the combination provides us with expanded capabilities across 
multiple industry verticals and service lines, more balanced geographic mix 
across North America, Europe and rest of the world, strengthened near-
shore European delivery footprint with presence across Romania, Portugal, 
Hungary and Poland, and positions us nicely as a truly global partner for 
large transformation programs with our global 2000 customers and 
prospects. This is further backed by strong cultural alignment between the 
two organizations anchored in entrepreneurial ethos and engineering-first 
culture and decades of trust with marquee clients. We are confident that 
this combination positions Persistent and Nagarro for the next chapter of 
sustained profitable growth together.  
Let me now provide you with the progress made since the last quarter in 
terms of the process as some of you may be tracking the closure timelines 
closely. Starting with the open offer update. The initial acceptance period 
for voluntary public takeover offer for Nagarro began on August 6th, 2026 
and ended on September 17th. The additional acceptance period began on 
September 23rd and ended on October 6th. We have secured 
approximately 94.04% of Nagarro share capital excluding treasury shares 
at the expiry of the additional acceptance period, significantly exceeding 
the minimum acceptance threshold of 50% + 1  share that we had set. 
Having secured more than 90% of Nagarro share capital and voting rights, 
we intend doing a squeeze out of the remaining minority shareholders of 
Nagarro upon closing.  
From a merger control clearance perspective, we have received all merger 
control clearances and all FDI clearances other than Austria and Spain. We 
are confident of getting these approvals in over the next several weeks. We

Persistent Systems Limited 
 
 
Page 6 of 25 
 
have also submitted the application for Reserve Bank of India's approval 
and we are following the due process to get the approval thereof. 
In terms of financing, we intend replacing the Euro 1.4 billion 18-month 
bridge loan with longer tenure, capital and favorable terms. As a part of 
this long-term financing strategy, we will be raising USD 1.25 billion in 
terms of both debt and equity. Out of this, USD 450 million will be raised 
through equity, qualified institutional placement or equity-linked 
instruments like FCCB or combination of similar instruments. We have 
received the shareholder approval for the above funding mix at the 
Extraordinary General Meeting held on October 5th. We sincerely believe 
that the combined persistent Nagarro group presents a significant value 
creation opportunity for all our shareholders, clients, partners and 
employees.  
As a part of this acquisition, I would like to highlight an important aspect 
around one-time expenses related to the transaction. Overall, we are 
expecting one-time expenses to the tune of approximately $50 million 
spread over three to four quarters. These expenses will weigh in on the 
reported EPS growth as you would have seen in our Q2 results reflecting 
an impact of around 3.1% on our reported PAT. We will be accounting for 
these expenses as they occur and will inform you all as we incur these 
expenses.  
Also, as you may be aware, our ESOP vesting criteria for our team members 
is conditional on achieving a 12% revenue growth and a 12% EPS growth. 
In line with this, the Board may seek shareholders' approval to treat these 
one-time transaction related expenses as an exception when assessing the 
ESOP vesting conditions.  
To summarize, all the processes related to the Nagarro acquisition are 
going on at the expected pace. We expect the deal closure by Q4-CY26 or 
Q1-CY27. We will keep you posted on the progress of this over time. We 
would like to place again on record our appreciation for Nagarro's 
Management Board as well as its Supervisory Board for their ongoing 
support and cooperation in the acquisition process. We are enthusiastic 
and look forward to working jointly with them and our extended Nagarro 
team to make this combination successful for all our stakeholders over 
time.  
With this, I would like to invite Vinit, our CFO, to provide more details on 
our financials for the quarter. Vinit, over to you.

Persistent Systems Limited 
 
 
Page 7 of 25 
 
 
Vinit Teredesai: 
Thank you, Sandeep. Good morning and good day to all. Thank you for 
taking the time to join us today. Let me now take you through the financial 
highlights for the quarter.  
Q2 FY27 revenue stood at USD 487.6 million, registering a year-on-year 
growth of 20%. In rupee terms, it translates to Rs.46,639 million, a growth 
of 30.3% year-on-year. EBIT for this quarter was Rs.6,977.2 million, 
translating to a growth of 19.5% year-on-year. EBIT margins for Q2 FY27 
came in at 15%, 130 basis points declined year-on-year. 
I will now talk about some operational updates for this quarter. At the end 
of Q2 FY27, our total headcount stood at 29,598, an increase of 958 from 
previous the quarter. Utilization stood at 85.8%, down 70 basis 
sequentially, primarily reflecting proactive hiring to support the ramp-up 
of large deals. Trailing 12-months attrition stood at 11.9% compared to 
12.3% in the previous quarter.  
Let me now give you quarter-on-quarter EBIT margin walkthrough. First, 
headwinds: As you would remember, this is the quarter when we have the 
yearly wage hike coming into effect. This impacted our margins by 180 
basis points. However, lower ESOP costs enabled us to absorb part of this 
impact, leaving us with a net impact of 140 basis points. Lower utilization 
led to a 20 basis impact on our EBIT margins. 
The large deal that we have announced in the previous quarter included 
end-to-end takeover of the engineering roadmap of portfolio of 20 
products across development, sustenance engineering, customer support, 
along with associated third-party licenses and cloud spend. This investment 
in the third-party tools and licenses led to an increase in the quarterly 
amortization of approximately USD 4 million, which had an impact of 90 
basis points on our Q2 EBIT margin. The plan is to leverage FinOps and AI-
led engineering roadmap to optimize the spend across people, tools, and 
cloud infrastructure in this large deal going forward. As we optimize the 
spend and our revenue scales in future, the impact on our margins will 
gradually reduce.  
Tailwinds: Lower ESOP SG&A expenses and favorable currency moments 
delivered a combined EBIT benefit of 150 basis points. Net impact taken 
together these headwinds and tailwinds resulted in a 100 basis point 
quarter-on-quarter decline in EBIT margin.

Persistent Systems Limited 
 
 
Page 8 of 25 
 
In respect of our treasury income, we had mark-to-market losses on our 
investment during the quarter of Rs. 116.4 million as against mark-to-
market gain of Rs. 146.7 million in the previous quarter. During the quarter, 
we had higher finance charges on account of higher receivables financing. 
The net result of both lower treasury income and higher finance costs 
resulted in negative net other income of Rs. 131.2 million as against a 
positive income of Rs. 414.9 million in the previous quarter.  
The foreign exchange loss was Rs. 455.8 million as against Rs. 1,052.7 
million in the previous quarter. Forward contracts outstanding as of 30th 
September, 2026 were USD 500 million at an average rate of 95.6 per 
dollar.  
Effective tax rate for the quarter came in at 22.5%, same as last quarter. 
Operating profit after tax for the quarter was Rs. 4,951.5 million, margin of 
10.6% with a year-on-year growth of 5%.  
We incurred transaction costs worth Rs. 1,853.4 million towards the 
Nagarro acquisition in this quarter. These expenses include transaction and 
advisory costs related to regulatory filing, financing charges, legal, 
communication and travel expenses. Over the next two quarters, we 
expect an incremental amount ranging between USD 25 to 30 million to be 
incurred towards the Nagarro transaction.  
For Q2 FY27, these expenses impacted the reported PAT margin as well as 
the reported EPS by around 3.1%. Reported profit after tax for the quarter 
was Rs. 3,515.1 million, a margin of 7.5%, with year-on-year decline of 
25.4%. Operating earnings per share was Rs. 31.6 with a year-on-year 
growth of 4.2%, whereas the reported earnings per share was at Rs. 22.4 
which translates into decline of 26%. Excluding cash from the capital 
employed, return on capital employed for Q2 FY27 came in at 45.6% versus 
43.6% in the previous quarter.  
We are happy to report that we had record collections during the quarter 
which helped to improve the cash position in spite of payment of final 
dividend and exceptional expenses related to Nagarro transactions. Total 
cash and investments stood at Rs. 29,996.7 million, around $315 million as 
of September 30, 2026 as against Rs. 27,044 million at the end of the 
previous quarter.  
Higher collections also helped reduce the billed DSO as well as led to the 
higher OCF to PAT for the quarter. The billed DSO decreased to 50 days as 
against 61 days in the previous quarter, while the unbilled DSO came in at

Persistent Systems Limited 
 
 
Page 9 of 25 
 
24 days as against 25 days in Q1 FY27. On TTM basis, trailing 12-months 
basis, OCF to PAT improved to 96.6% in Q2 FY27 compared to 76.2% in the 
previous quarter.  
Coming to updates on ESG. Sustainability continues to be integrated into 
Persistent’s business strategy with a focus on managing risk, improving 
operational efficiency and delivering measurable ESG outcomes.  
• Our commitment to ESG excellence was reflected in an improved 
ESG score of 83.3 from SES, a semi-registered ESG rating provider 
for FY25-26, up from 81.7 in the prior year, underscoring continued 
progress in the execution of our sustainability strategy.  
• We are proud to have received a jury mention in the Climate Action 
and Carbon Neutrality Leadership category at the Sustainable 
World Awards 2026 by BW Business World.  
• Persistent Systems Pune has also been recognized as the winner of 
the Decarbonization Excellence Award 2026 in the Net Zero Carbon 
category at the CoOL Conclave by ISHRAE.  
• We are also proud to be recognized as one of America's greatest 
workplaces in Tech 2026 by Newsweek.  
These achievements reinforce the progress we are making in embedding 
sustainability across our operations, climate action and people practices, 
while continuing to strengthen our overall ESG performance.  
With this, let me now hand over to Nitish for commentary on our progress 
on the AI journey. Nitish, over to you.  
Nitish Shrivastava: 
Thank you, Vinit. Good morning and good day to everyone. As we shared 
on our last call, our AI strategy continues to rest on three pillars, 
engineering 
hyper-productivity, 
business 
hyper-productivity 
and 
enterprise data readiness with responsible AI. We believe the next phase 
of enterprise AI will be defined not by better models alone, but by how well 
enterprises combine them with their own knowledge, data processes, 
people and governance. We call this The Enterprise Context and our 3C 
architecture of core context and coordination is how we help our clients 
build it.  
Last quarter, we enhanced our software engineering productivity offering 
with the launch of Software Reinvention Services, a new offering aimed at 
helping enterprise software companies accelerate their next generation 
products, while improving the economics of the products they run today.

Persistent Systems Limited 
 
 
Page 10 of 25 
 
Software companies are facing challenges on two fronts. On one hand, they 
are facing challenges on growth as AI native companies and model 
providers compete for their customers. On the other hand, they are facing 
challenges on cost as their established products must generate the margin 
to fund AI investment, while the AI consumptions add a new and fast rising 
cost. Software Reinvention Services addresses both: 
Starting with growth. On growth, we are helping our clients build new 
products faster and take them to market faster. For new product 
development, we are focused on speed and quality. We deliver AI-led 
development acceleration through our SASVA platform. SASVA runs on our 
custom tuned models and also work with models from Anthropic, OpenAI 
and leading open-source providers which gives our client flexibility in their 
choice of models. Clients can adopt our AI stack as a complete platform or 
deploy it alongside their existing AI tools where it adds measurement, 
collaboration and structured ways of working.  
We are now working with our client's product managers to prioritize the 
features most likely to achieve product fit in the market. In recent 
programs for software companies, this approach has helped bring product-
to-market about 50% faster. For go-to-market, we are helping our clients 
reach and win customers faster. Together with a leading private equity 
firm, we are building an AI-powered go-to-market harness to help software 
companies reach their customers faster.  
Additionally, in select cases, we are building products with our clients in a 
co-sell motion. Our AI-led professional services model is turning into 
delivery expertise by getting our client's customer life sooner and 
improving time-to-market by more than 25%.  
On cost, our focus is on improving the economics of client's established 
product because the margin from established products fund the forward-
looking AI growth. These products carry years of accumulated cost and we 
apply AI across the full cost of ownership in three distinct areas:  
First, we are running mature product through the AI-led sustenance and 
helping our client carve out products outside their core. For example, for 
one marquee software company, we have taken over several product lines 
in data operation, data governance, and endpoint management. We are 
now running their engineering sustenance and go-to-market, while 
reducing their cost of running these products by 45%.

Persistent Systems Limited 
 
 
Page 11 of 25 
 
Second, we are helping clients bring cloud and AI consumption fast under 
control. We are combining cloud optimization with AI-led engineering and 
FinOps to reduce cloud consumption and operating cost. Our tokenomics 
offering and  Sasva’sintelligent model routing, which matches each task to 
the most suitable model, are keeping token cost under control.  
Third, we are reducing both labour and non-labour spend across SG&A. On 
the non-labour side, we are re-architecting products and replacing long-tail 
tools with custom agentic applications to lower third-party license cost. On 
the labour side, we are bringing agentic system into SG&A and automating 
workflows across IT, HR, finance, and procurement. Our clients are, in turn, 
reinvesting these savings into new products and go-to-market so cost 
efficiency becomes fuel for growth.  
A strong validation of Software Reinvention Services is the large deal we 
signed last quarter, a 6.5-year engagement worth more than $650 million 
with one of the largest technology companies spanning product 
development support and cloud operations across multiple SaaS products.  
Our position in the market is built on long product engineering experience. 
Over 36 years, we have engineered products for more than 300 software 
companies, and today we are serving nine of the top 10 technology 
companies. Through Accelerite, we have also operated our own software 
product business, which gave us the direct experience in building, selling, 
supporting, and sustaining enterprise software. We are now turning that 
experience into a repeatable playbook that combines our platform, 
partners' ecosystem, and accelerators.  
Software Reinvention Services is drawing on the same platform and 
capabilities that are powering our broader AI strategies, and the same 
disciplined approach is continuing to deliver results across our three pillars. 
The quarter gone by, we continue to expand our partnerships by becoming 
a preferred partner in Anthropic's cloud partner network services track and 
earning Microsoft's agentic business solution specialization. Our teams 
today hold nearly 25,000 partner certifications across Microsoft, AWS, 
Google Cloud, Salesforce, Databricks, and Snowflakes, and have earned 
more than 58,000 AI certifications to date.  
In summary, as models commoditize, enterprise software differentiation is 
shifting to the context around them and to the economics of the product 
the clients already run. We are helping clients build new products, fund 
them from the products they run today, and bring them faster to the 
market. We are turning that work into a durable, client-owned asset and

Persistent Systems Limited 
 
 
Page 12 of 25 
 
applying the same playbook across engagements. This is where Persistent 
is continuing to invest and where we see long-term value for our clients 
and our shareholders.  
I will now invite Saurabh to share other key wins and awards for the 
quarter.  
Saurabh Dwivedi: 
Thank you, Nitish. Let me now talk about the most important deal wins for 
the quarter by industry segments. 
Starting off with Software High-Tech and Emerging Industry vertical. A 
leading hyperscaler has selected Persistent as a preferred partner for its 
newly formed forward-deployed engineering organization to scale legacy 
modernization and transformation programs. Our dedicated, certified FDE 
team will work alongside the hyperscalers' forward-deployed engineers as 
an extension of its delivery capacity, embedding directly with customers to 
modernize and platformize mainframe and legacy states across industries. 
These engagements are anchored in business outcomes rather than effort, 
providing customers with a faster, lower risk path from legacy systems to 
AI-ready platforms.  
Moving on to Banking, Financial Services and Insurance. A Fortune 500 US 
insurer has selected Persistent as its AI-led modernization partner for its 
personal lines policy administration. The business was running critical 
underwriting, rating, and renewal processes on a legacy core platform, 
which was leading to inefficiencies and higher costs. Our engagement with 
the customer involves rebuilding a modern, cloud-native policy 
administration platform.  
The first phase of the programme, powered by our proprietary AI 
accelerators, will demonstrate a repeatable, automated path from legacy 
to modern architecture. Subsequent phases will reduce operating costs, 
accelerate product and pricing rollouts, retire legacy spend, and expand 
into adjacent lines of business. 
Now, coming to our Healthcare and Lifesciences vertical. One of the largest 
cancer research and treatment organisations in the US has chosen 
Persistent to manage their technology that supports cancer care across its 
national network. As part of the engagement, we will bring clinical 
applications, enterprise systems, data and infrastructure under a single 
delivery model, while providing on-site support at care locations. We will 
leverage AI to capture critical knowledge, ensuring that patients and 
clinicians experience minimal disruption during the transition. Our

Persistent Systems Limited 
 
 
Page 13 of 25 
 
oncology and revenue cycle expertise will help the client deliver more 
consistent care across its locations.  
Now coming to the key awards and recognitions we received during the 
quarter. Persistent continued to receive multiple leadership recognitions 
from ISG in this quarter and received 6 awards at the ISG (Information 
Services Group) “Provider Lens Awards 2026”. The recognitions span 
Digital Engineering, AI, Cloud ecosystems, Cyber Security and Industry 
Services demonstrating the depth of expertise across Persistent. Persistent 
was recognized as for the second year in a row achieve the growth honour 
of the year in annual revenue more than USD 1 to 5 billion category at 
“Everest Group Elevate 2026”. Persistent received multiple awards for its 
commitment to ESG and people excellence. The most prominent amongst 
them included “Persistent one Business World Sustainable World's Award 
2026” in the climate action and carbon neutrality leadership category. 
Persistent was also honoured across 7 categories at the “People Matters 
Infinity Awards India 2026” for excellence in talent and employee 
experience.  
With this let me hand it back to Sandeep. 
Sandeep Kalra: 
Thank you, Saurabh. Let me conclude the prepared remarks by saying that 
we are happy with the consistent performance we have been able to 
deliver this quarter. The consistency of execution quarter after quarter is 
the testament to disciplined execution along with our clear strategy. We 
are making good progress on our AI capability build, client engagements 
as well as our Nagarro acquisition. I'd like to sincerely thank our 
employees, clients, partners and shareholders for their strong support and 
sustained confidence in us.

Every generation of technology arrives with 
a promise. The promise of AI is the most 
consequential in decades, and this time, the 
potential is real. AI can reshape how organisations 
build software, serve customers, manage risk, 
accelerate discovery and make decisions. The 
investments are justified. The urgency is warranted. 
What is also real is this: many organisations are 
struggling to translate that promise into measurable 
impact. It is not because they lack access to 
models, platforms or ambition. The distance 
between AI strategy and operational reality, 
between boardroom commitment and production 
deployment is wider, more structurally complex 
and harder to close than many anticipated. Pilots 
that proved the concept have stalled before 
production. Data that seemed ready has turned 
out to be fragmented, inconsistent or ungoverned. 
Agents that performed well in demonstrations 
have struggled in the messy, regulated and 
interconnected reality of large organisations. 
The gap is real and it is costing organisations time, 
capital and competitive ground. 
More fundamentally, AI is reshaping how 
organisations create value, compete and grow. 
The next competitive advantage will come from the 
ability to integrate intelligence into the operating 
core of the organisation. The organisations that 
succeed will not simply adopt AI. They will redesign 
how work gets done around it. 
This is the moment Persistent was built for. 
We chose this year's theme, Re(AI)magining™ the 
Enterprise: Where AI Ambition Meets Engineering 
Execution, not to describe an aspiration, but to 
define where we create value. Persistent sits at 
the point where AI strategy becomes operational 
reality and where lasting advantage is created. That 
standing is earned, not claimed. 
Persistent's heritage in software and product 
engineering places us at the intersection of AI, 
data and modernisation. For more than three 
decades, we have helped clients engineer complex 
technology systems that are resilient, scalable and 
business-critical. Those strengths are becoming 
increasingly relevant as organisations move from 
experimentation towards widespread adoption. 
They are reflected in our AI platforms, SASVA™, 
iAURA and GenAI Hub, and in the 3C Framework 
of Core, Context and Coordination. Together, they 
help organisations establish a strong technology 
foundation, apply intelligence with business context 
and embed AI into the workflows where decisions 
and outcomes are created. Importantly, these 
are not frameworks designed for presentation 
slides. They are disciplines built through real-world 
deployment, refined within Persistent as Customer 
Zero and applied across increasingly complex client 
environments. That experience continues to shape 
how we help clients move from fragmented AI 
investments to trusted outcomes. 
The organisations we serve are at an inflection 
point. AI ambition is funded. The question now 
is execution. 
The next phase belongs to organisations capable 
of turning pilots into platforms, data into insight 
and governance into a foundation for growth. The 
winners will be those that can embed intelligence 
into the systems, workflows and decisions that drive 
business performance. This is where Persistent 
stands apart. We bring the engineering depth, data 
foundation, platform IP, governance discipline and 
delivery model required to help clients move from 
investment to measurable, trusted outcomes.
FY26 showed what becomes possible when AI 
ambition meets engineering execution. This report 
is the story of that progress and the foundation for 
what comes next.

At Persistent, ESG is not a parallel agenda 
but a core enabler of long-term resilience, 
responsible growth and stakeholder trust. 
As technology reshapes industries and 
societies, we believe enterprises that 
combine innovation with accountability 
and growth with stewardship will define 
responsible leadership in the AI era, resulting 
in strengthened operational resilience, 
responsible decision-making and enduring 
trust with clients, partners, investors 
and communities.
As a UN Global Compact participant, with 
Net Zero 2050 targets approved by the 
Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi), we 
remain aligned with globally recognised 
frameworks and climate science.
During FY26, we translated ESG 
commitments into measurable progress. 
We achieved a 62.90% reduction in market-
based emissions and a 20.20% reduction 
in location-based emissions across Scope 
1, 2 and 3 (from the FY24 baseline), while 
sustaining carbon neutrality for Scope 1 and 
Scope 2 emissions for the third year in

from 56.83% to 68.22%, with India-owned

India-owned operations, along with 100% 
wastewater recycling, an 11.01% reduction 
in freshwater consumption, and plantation 
of nearly two lakh trees through Persistent 
Foundation initiatives.
Governance remains central to our approach. 
We strengthened oversight through a double 
materiality assessment integrated into our 
Enterprise Risk Management framework and 
established a value-chain reporting process 
aligned with SEBI's BRSR requirements. As AI 
adoption accelerates, we believe responsible 
innovation must remain closely tied to 
transparency, ethics and human impact.

Policy Compliance - Code of Conduct. Our

top 10% of IT services companies in the S&P 
Global Sustainability Yearbook 2026.
Looking ahead, we remain focused on 
deepening ESG integration across strategy, 
operations and value chains, balancing 
innovation, governance and societal impact 
to build durable long-term value.

Report of the Directors
Your Directors are pleased to present the Thirty-sixth Annual Report of your Company along with the Audited 
Financial Statements for the Financial Year ended March 31, 2026.
A. Business Update
The theme of this year’s report, Re(AI)magining the Enterprise, reflects both the moment our industry has reached 
and the role your Company has chosen within it. Across the world, enterprises are rethinking how they operate, 
transform, and compete in the presence of Artificial Intelligence. Ambition is everywhere; what remains scarce is the 
engineering execution to turn that ambition into something impactful, governed, and measurable. That intersection, 
where AI ambition meets engineering execution, is where your Company does its most consequential work.
It is also where Persistent has always operated. For thirty-six years, your Company has been built not around any 
single technology wave but around a more enduring belief that a company stays valuable by continuing to learn, 
adapt, and earn its customers’ trust through every cycle of change. AI is the latest and most far-reaching of those 
cycles, and one that rewards precisely the strengths your Company has spent decades cultivating, which include 
engineering judgement, technical depth, and the discipline to execute responsibly at scale.
Your Company entered this moment having built capability ahead of demand, and Financial Year 2025-26 reflected 
the payoff. In Financial Year 2025-26, Revenue was US$ 1,654.4 Million, growing 17.4% Year-on-Year in US$ terms 
and 23.5% in Indian Rupee terms, strengthening your Company’s standing among the fastest-growing companies 
in the industry. Q4FY 26 marked the 24th consecutive quarter of sequential growth; a cadence achieved by only a 
handful of companies. Profitability strengthened even as the Company continued to invest ahead of demand, full-year 
EBIT margin expanded to 15.6%, and Profit After Tax rose 33% to INR 18,651 Million, with the fourth-quarter EBIT 
margin reaching 16.3%. On the strength of this performance, the Board recommended a final dividend of INR 18 per 
share, bringing the total dividend for the year to INR 40 per share, up from INR 35 per share a year earlier, subject to 
shareowners’ approval. As AI adoption accelerated, your Company’s AI-led, platform-driven approach strengthened 
its operating model from within, improving the quality, velocity, and scale of everything it delivers. The defining lesson 
of the year, visible across every industry, is that success with AI depends less on the sophistication of any single model 
than on operational maturity, including clean, well-governed data, redesigned processes, an enabled workforce, and 
responsible governance. Enterprises are no longer seeking a vendor of AI features; they are seeking a partner who can 
make AI work safely, repeatably, and accountably, inside the systems on which their business already runs. That is the 
role your Company has built itself to play: through a model that is platform-centric, IP-led, and outcome-based, and in 
which it is consistently its own first customer.
Across its three industry verticals, Software, Hi-Tech and Emerging Industries; Banking, Financial Services and 
Insurance; and Healthcare and Life Sciences, this strategy is advancing on several reinforcing fronts:
•	
Engineering Hyper Productivity. Your Company’s Generative AI-enabled engineering platform, SASVA, reached 
its fourth generation, with SASVA 4.0 becoming generally available in April 2026 and backed by a portfolio of 
more than 120 patents. Shifting the focus from individual productivity to team intelligence, its “Brain” holds the 
full organisational context and validates workflows by simulation before execution, while integration with partner 
models, frontier models such as Anthropic’s Claude and OpenAI’s GPT, lets clients bring their own model of 
choice and tooling into a single, governed environment that accelerates software development and reduces 
technical debt at scale.
•	
Business Hyper Productivity. Your Company is reimagining end-to-end business workflows as self-orchestrating 
ecosystems of AI agents. During the year it enhanced its GenAI Hub and Agent Studio, launched an Agent 
Processing Unit to onboard and orchestrate external agents, and grew its portfolio to more than 250 enterprise 
agents with deep domain coverage across BFSI and Healthcare and Life Sciences.
•	
Enterprise Data Readiness. Trusted, contextual and governed data is the foundation of scaled enterprise AI 
readiness and adoption. To accelerate this journey, your Company enhanced its iAURA platform with a modern 
interface, agentified Data Engineering Lifecycle, and an AI Data Mapper and Modeller grounded in a semantic 
layer. A new Enterprise Data Assessment capability builds knowledge graphs and enterprise data context, 
capturing business meaning, relationships, and domain knowledge, giving AI agents the memory to act with 
precision. A Cost of Intelligence capability brings governance, making AI spend measurable and accountable, 
giving enterprises the trusted foundations on which durable AI value is built.

Policy for the appointment of a new director on the Board
The Board of Directors decides the criteria for the appointment of a new director on the Board from time to time 
depending on the dates of retirement of existing Directors and the strategic needs of your Company. The criteria 
include expertise area, industry experience, professional background, association with other companies, and similar 
important parameters.
Once the criteria are determined, the Board directs the NRC to compile profiles of suitable candidates through 
networking, industry associations and business connections. The NRC considers these profiles on the decided 
parameters and shortlists the candidates.
For every new member to be added, at least three members of the NRC interact with the panel of candidates.  
The panel consists of at least two to four potential candidates.
Efforts are made to ensure that the Board has adequate diversity across various parameters such as nationality, 
expertise and gender in terms of the Board Diversity Policy. The Board has decided that for every position of the 
Board, at least one female candidate will be part of the shortlisted panel of candidates for consideration.
The Board Diversity Policy adopted by the Board sets out its approach to diversity. The policy is available on the

behalf. Your Company has appointed M/s. MUFG Intime India Private Limited (formerly known as Link Intime India Private 
Limited) (‘MUFG Intime’) to manage the share and dividend management process. They have created a facility for online 
submission of Tax Exemption forms where the Members can submit their tax-exemption forms along with other required

as below: https://web.in.mpms.mufg.com/client-downloads.html → On this page, select the General tab. All the forms are 
available under the head “Form 121 / Form 41”.
Kindly note that Form 121 is a newly introduced Form by the Income Tax Department replacing the earlier Forms 15G and 
15H. Now, both types of taxpayers, i.e., those below the age of 60 and those aged 60 and above, will use Form No. 121 to 
submit a declaration to avoid relevant income from being subjected to TDS.
Further, please note that Form 41 is required to be filed by non-resident taxpayers. This form is also a newly introduced 
form and has replaced earlier Form 10F. It must be filed when a non-resident wants to claim relief under a Double Taxation 
Avoidance Agreement (DTAA) as provided in Section 159 of the Income Tax Act, 1961 as amended from time to time.
The aforementioned forms (duly completed and signed) are required to be uploaded on the following URL:

IEPFA, under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA), launched the 100 Day Campaign titled ‘Saksham Niveshak’

Education and Protection Fund (IEPF).

transfers to the IEPF.

The Board of Directors of your Company has developed a Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Policy to serve as 
a framework for guiding the Company’s CSR initiatives. This policy is publicly accessible and can be viewed on the 
Company’s official website at CSR Policy.pdf
	
The CSR Policy outlines the belief that as a responsible Company, employing a large number of employees, 
it is the Company’s obligation to contribute to society and the community. The Company has held this belief 
since inception. The journey began in 1995 when the Board decided to commit 1% of profits for social causes. 
The allocation was subsequently increased to 2% following the introduction of the CSR provisions under the 
Companies Act, 2013.
	
While there are many projects that need CSR support, a more impactful contribution can be achieved by focusing 
on specific areas. Accordingly, your Company has decided to focus CSR activities, in four areas:
	
1.	 Health,
	
2.	 Education,
	
3.	 Community Development, and
	
4.	 Wildlife and Heritage Conservation
	
Your Company started the CSR journey in 1995, and the Company formalised its CSR efforts by establishing 
a Public Charitable Trust, Persistent Foundation, during the Financial Year 2008-09. In line with the evolving 
regulatory framework and to further strengthen governance and execution of CSR activities, the Company 
incorporated Persistent India Foundation, a Section 8 Company under the Companies Act, 2013, on May 1, 2024.
	
During the year under Report, the CSR projects of the Company were implemented through Persistent India 
Foundation (the ‘Foundation’) and few other eligible partnering Non-Government Organisations (NGO).
	
Further, as part of its efforts to extend its CSR approach to geographies, your Company established Persistent 
Systems Foundation Inc., a 501(c) no-profit corporation in the United States, during the FY 2022-23. The US 
Foundation received the requisite tax exemption approvals during the FY 2024-25. During the FY 2025-26, 
the Company undertook CSR initiatives through the US Foundation, aligned with its CSR philosophy of 
contributing to the communities it serves and its commitment to undertake socially responsible activities in a 
structured manner beyond statutory requirements.
	
In addition to the impact of the project funded, the Foundation considers the extent to which Persistent’s 
employees can contribute to socially relevant projects. Persistent believes in the culture of giving and contributing 
and all employees are encouraged to participate in CSR activities of the Foundation.

Community Development – Livelihood Project
Wildlife and Heritage conservation — Rooting advancement in our cultural and natural inheritance
As part of its commitment to protecting wildlife and maintaining ecological balance, the Foundation supported 
the use of technology to strengthen conservation efforts and reduce conflict between humans and wildlife. Drone 
cameras were deployed to track the movement of wild animals and monitor forest areas. These drones were also used 
for tiger census activities and to observe elephant movement in sensitive corridors. This enabled timely monitoring, 
better coordination on the ground, and quicker response to potential risks.
These efforts support the forest department in safeguarding wildlife habitats and help create awareness among local 
communities. By providing early alerts and reliable tracking information, the initiatives play an important role in preventing 
human-wildlife conflict and improving safety for both people and animals.
Alongside wildlife conservation, the Foundation also supported heritage preservation and public education by contributing to 
the upkeep and improvement of museum infrastructure. This included maintenance work and upgrades to essential facilities, 
enabling effective use of audio guide systems for visitors.
Infrastructure support was also extended to Shivsrushti, a historic theme park in Pune, where digital display screens were 
installed to enhance storytelling and provide visitors with a more engaging and educational experience through immersive 
visual content.
In line with its CSR commitment to wildlife care, the Foundation also supported the operations of an aviary providing medical 
treatment to injured and rescued birds. During the year, 673 birds across six species received care, of which 509 were 
successfully rehabilitated and released back into their natural habitats. These efforts contributed meaningfully to biodiversity 
conservation and the restoration of local ecosystems.

Employee Engagement
At the Foundation, employee engagement is at the heart of its CSR efforts, reflecting a culture where employees 
voluntarily contribute their time, skills, and care to support communities. Through well-structured volunteering 
opportunities across education, health, environment, and community development, employees are encouraged to 
participate actively and create meaningful social impact.
During the year, employee volunteering continued to see strong participation. A total of 5,841 employees contributed 
11,683 hours across 70 initiatives. Overall, 299 volunteering activities were conducted across 15 locations, reflecting 
broad participation and geographic reach.
Volunteering programmes were designed to be inclusive and flexible, enabling employees across roles and locations 
to participate alongside their regular work commitments. On average, each volunteer contributed close to two hours, 
reflecting consistent and high quality engagement. Locations such as Pune, Nagpur, Hyderabad, and Goa recorded

In addition to volunteering, employees actively supported the Foundation through donation drives, further 
strengthening the culture of giving. Employee contributions during the year amounted to INR 47.12 lakh, 
supplemented by INR 34.79 lakh from other sources. Together, these contributions played an important role in 
strengthening the Foundation’s social programmes and extending their reach.

Report on Corporate Governance
Company’s beliefs on Corporate Governance
“Corporate governance is concerned with holding the balance between economic and social goals and aligning the 
interests of individuals, corporations and society.”
- Sir Adrian Cadbury
Redefining Stakeholders for a Sustainable Future
Traditionally, the stakeholders of a public limited company have been defined in legal terms, comprising shareholders, 
debenture-holders, deposit-holders, and other security holders. While such a definition remains relevant, the 
Company believes that in the context of a modern and evolving business environment, the scope of stakeholders 
must extend far beyond statutory classifications.
At Persistent, we recognise that long-term value creation is intrinsically linked with the interests of all those 
who contribute to, and are impacted by, our operations. Accordingly, our approach to stakeholder engagement 
encompasses not only our investors, but also our employees and their families, customers, business partners, vendors, 
regulators, and the communities and ecosystems within which we operate.
In line with this philosophy, the Board of Directors has affirmed a broader and more inclusive definition of 
stakeholders. This approach aligns with the Company’s sustainability vision and reinforces its commitment to creating 
shared and enduring value for all stakeholder groups.
Our Commitment to Responsible Governance
Corporate Governance is a fundamental cornerstone of our operations and is anchored in the principles of trust, 
transparency, and accountability. Our governance framework is designed to balance the interests of a diverse 
stakeholder base while enabling robust and ethical decision-making that supports sustainable business growth.
Integrity, inclusivity, and sustainability are fundamental to the Company’s corporate culture. Through continuous 
enhancement of governance practices, we strive to uphold the highest standards of accountability while contributing 
positively to the broader economic, social, and environmental ecosystem.
This section presents an overview of how the Company engages with stakeholders, integrates Environmental, Social, 
and Governance (ESG) considerations into strategy, and seeks to deliver long-term sustainable value. 
1.	
Employees and their Families 
	
The Company’s continued success is driven by the expertise, commitment, and dedication of employees. 
Senior employees play a critical role in shaping the Company’s strategic direction and overseeing operations. 
Recognising the vital support extended by employees’ families, the Company remains committed to safeguarding 
their overall well-being.
2.	 Clients
	
The Company provides services to its clients because of which we earn our revenue. Their satisfaction and delight 
are important focus areas of the Company’s operations. Our clients are keen that we succeed and continue to 
deliver on our promises and hence, they are also vested in our success.
3.	 Partners
	
The Company collaborates with its partners to deliver value to its clients. These relationships are built on mutual 
trust and shared objectives. The Company believes that the strength and success of its partnerships are integral to 
its own growth and endeavours to support the long-term success of its partners.
4.	 Suppliers 
	
The Company relies on a network of suppliers for various goods and services essential to its operations. Operational 
efficiency is closely linked to the quality and reliability of these contributions. The Company is committed to 
maintaining fair and sustainable relationships with its suppliers and supporting their long-term growth.

5.	 Shareowners/Investors 
	
Shareowners are the owners of the Company and are the traditional stakeholders in the Company. They have 
invested in the Company, and we believe it is our responsibility to deliver fair returns to our shareowners.
6.	 Environment
	
It is a constant endeavour of the Company to conserve and preserve the environment. Over the years, the Company 
has focused on sustainable business practices encompassing economic, environmental, and social imperatives. The 
Company also works through Persistent Foundation and Persistent India Foundation, to support projects in the areas of 
environmental sustainability and ecological balance. 
	
To maintain and strengthen relationships with its stakeholders, the Company has established structured 
mechanisms and governance processes. The Company remains aligned with global sustainability goals and 
continues to monitor and enhance its performance against ESG metrics.
	
Stakeholder relationships are managed through clearly defined roles and responsibilities across the organisation. 
The Board of Directors and leadership teams periodically review these activities to ensure adherence to the highest 
standards of governance.
	
The Nomination and Remuneration Committee (‘NRC’) oversees matters relating to employees, while the Stakeholders’ 
Relationship and ESG Committee (‘SRC’) is entrusted with addressing the interests of investors, shareholders, and 
other security holders in accordance with applicable laws. The Company has also brought ESG oversight within the 
purview of the SRC to ensure focused Board-level attention to sustainability initiatives.
	
To enable a coordinated approach to stakeholder engagement, the SRC receives inputs from management and other 
relevant committees and prepares an annual report for submission to the Board. This report forms an integral part of 
the Company’s disclosures.
	
The Company believes that strong Corporate Governance practices are essential for enhancing long-term stakeholder 
value. Continuous improvement in governance standards remains a key priority, enabling the Company to build trust, 
strengthen resilience, and support sustainable growth.
	
This Report on Corporate Governance reflects the Company’s ongoing commitment to adhering to governance 
principles in both letter and spirit, while striving to maintain the highest standards of integrity and transparency.

d.	 Board Diversity 
	
	
The Company acknowledges and respects the significance of diverse representation on the Board for better 
decision-making and its growth and success. Diverse Board composition will enable the Company to assess 
issues through a broader lens, through differences in ideas and points of view. Board diversity is considered 
along these dimensions: global experience, cultural and geographical background, age, ethnicity, gender, 
sexual orientation, knowledge, and skills.
	
	
The Board Diversity Policy adopted by the Board sets out its approach to diversity. The policy is available on 
our website at http://www.persistent.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/Board-Diversity-Policy.pdf
	
e.	 Board Meetings and Deliberations
	
	
The Company Secretary, in consultation with the Chairman of the Board of Directors and the Chairpersons 
of the respective Board Committees, prepares the agenda and supporting documents for discussion at each 
Board / Committee meeting, respectively. Members of the Board or Committees may suggest items to be 
included in the agenda. In addition, they have the right to bring matters for discussion at the meeting with the 
permission of the Chairpersons.
	
	
Information and data that are important for the Board to understand the business of the Company and current 
affairs are tabled for discussion at the meeting. The agenda is circulated in writing to the members of the Board 
at least seven calendar days before the meeting in accordance with the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 
(the ‘Act’) and the Secretarial Standard – 1 (‘SS-1’) issued by the Institute of Company Secretaries of India.

The Chairman of the Board circulates a short Executive Summary that includes the following sections to the Board 
Members:
	
	
1.	 Highlights
	
	
2.	 Financial Summary
	
	
3.	 State of the Business
	
	
4.	 Items for Decisions in the Meeting
	
	
5.	 Items for Discussion
	
	
6.	 Items for the Board’s information
	
	
The Executive Summary helps the Board Members to stay focused on the most important items for the 
meeting.
	
	
The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) also circulates the highlights of the business performance of the Company 
for every quarter to the Board and the Committees in advance. This enables the Board and the Committees to 
provide focused guidance to the Management during the meetings.
	
	
The Board and the Audit Committee meet in executive sessions at least four times during a financial year, 
typically, in the third week of the first month of the quarter, inter alia, to review the financial statement of the 
immediate past quarter and other items on the agenda. Additional meetings are held, as deemed necessary, to 
conduct the business. Those members of the Board, who are not able to participate in the Board meetings in-
person participate through Video Conferencing (VC) / Other Audio Visual Means (OAVM) in accordance with 
provisions of Section 173(2) of the Act read with rule 3 of Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 
2014 and the Secretarial Standard – 1 (‘SS-1’) issued by the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (Including 
any statutory modification(s) or re-enactment thereof for the time being in force).
	
	
The Executives of the Company, such as Business Unit Heads, Chief People Officer, Chief Operating Officer, 
Chief Planning Officer, Chief Delivery Officer, Chief Marketing Officer, General Counsel, Chief Information 
Officer, etc., are invited as needed to participate in Board and Committee meetings. The other Senior 
Management Personnel and Delivery Heads are invited to the meetings on a need basis.

Board meetings must not exceed 120 (One Hundred and Twenty) days; the Company strictly follows this. The 
maximum gap between two Board meetings during the Financial Year 2025-26 was 97 (Ninety-Seven days), 
i.e., from October 14, 2025, to January 19, 2026, which is within the permissible time limit.

Performance Evaluation of the Board, its Committees and Individual Directors
	
	
The Company conducted the annual performance evaluation of the Board, the Chairman, its various 
Committees and the Directors individually, including the Independent Directors. In accordance with the 
provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015, the performance evaluation was undertaken with the assistance of an external management 
consultant specialising in Board evaluations.
	
	
The evaluation was carried out through a structured process covering various aspects of the Board’s 
functioning, including composition and structure, effectiveness of Board processes, quality and timeliness of 
information flow, engagement and participation in deliberations, strategic oversight, governance effectiveness, 
risk management and compliance, along with qualitative inputs and perspectives on the future direction of 
the Board and the Company. The performance of the Board was assessed through inputs obtained from all 
Directors and select senior management executives. 
	
	
The evaluation process also covered the performance of the Board Committees against the requirements of 
their respective charters and the effectiveness in discharging their responsibilities. The external consultant 
conducted one-on-one interactions with each Board Member to obtain detailed feedback.
	
	
The Board reviewed and discussed the outcomes of the evaluation in an executive session and noted that 
the Board, its Committees and the Directors, including the Independent Directors, continued to function 
effectively and demonstrated a high level of engagement, objectivity and preparedness in their roles. The 
evaluation process also enabled identification of areas for continuous improvement further improving overall 
Board effectiveness. The Board has taken note of these inputs and will address them as part of its ongoing 
governance and development initiatives.
	
	
The evaluation for FY 2025-26 was conducted in March and April 2026. The findings of the evaluation were 
presented at the meetings of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee and the Board of Directors held in 
April 2026.

Those Charged with Governance (TCWG) Committee
	
Your Company has constituted a ‘Those Charged with Governance (TCWG) Committee’ pursuant to the National 
Financial Reporting Authority (‘NFRA’) Circular dated January 7, 2026, with the framework becoming effective 
from April 1, 2026. TCWG comprises the Board of Directors, with the Audit Committee acting as a delegated sub-
group, along with key executives including the Chairman and Managing Director, Executive Directors (CEO and 
CFO), and the Company Secretary. TCWG is responsible for overseeing strategic direction, financial reporting, 
internal controls, audit matters, and ensuring appropriate escalation of significant issues such as fraud, going 
concern risks, and regulatory non-compliance to the Board. The Company has designated nodal persons from 
both sides to facilitate communication as follows:

Disclosures
Code of Conduct
Pursuant to the requirements of Regulation 17(5)(a) of Listing Regulations, the Company obtains the affirmation of compliance 
of the Code of Conduct from its Directors and Senior Management on a yearly basis since Financial Year 2005-06. 
Furthermore, the Code of Conduct applies to all the Company employees and its subsidiaries.
The Code of Conduct is an annual declaration that helps remind all employees and stakeholders the importance of maintaining 
the highest standards of ethical business conduct for the Company. In terms of the Code of Conduct, Directors and Employees 
must act within the guidelines of the authority conferred upon them and with a duty to make and enact informed decisions and 
policies in the best interests of the Company and its shareholders and stakeholders.
Further, Directors and Employees must ensure that they do not derive any undue personal benefit due to their position in the 
Company and from the access they have to certain confidential information coming to their knowledge.
It has been affirmed by the Board of Directors that the Code of Conduct has been complied with by all the Board members and 
all the Employees and a declaration to this effect forms part of this Report. The Code of Conduct is uploaded on the website of 
the Company at Code of Conduct for Directors and Employees | Persistent Systems 
In addition to the annual Code of Conduct, the Board has also established a robust Code of Conduct on Prevention of Insider 
Trading in terms of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015. The Company has a zero tolerance policy towards 
insider trading, corruption, bribery, and money laundering.
Familiarisation Program for the Board of Directors
Pursuant to the requirements of Regulation 25(7) of Listing Regulations, the Company conducts the Familiarisation Program for 
Independent Directors as well as other Directors on the Board about their roles, rights, responsibilities in the Company, nature of 
the industry in which the Company operates, business model of the Company, etc., through various initiatives. The Company 
also shares the organogram and important organisational changes on a regular basis. A few initiatives under familiarisation 
program are elaborated at https://www.persistent.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Familiarization-Programme-2025-26.
pdf
Board deliberations on strategy planning
As part of our annual strategy planning process, the Company organises sessions for the Board Members and Senior Executives 
to deliberate on various topics related to technological overview, global scenario for the IT industry, sales strategy, market 
research, risk overview, succession planning and strategic programs required to achieve the Company’s long-term objectives.
The Company organises periodic planning meetings called the ‘Huddle’, which is attended by all the senior sales and delivery 
leaders of the Organisation. Board Members participate in the Huddle to get a first-hand view of the strategy planning and 
implementation process and guide the leadership by offering their expertise.
This serves a dual purpose of providing a platform for Board Members to bring their expertise to the projects, while also 
providing an opportunity for them to understand detailed aspects of execution and challenges relating to the business of  
the Company.
Whistleblower Policy
The Board of Directors of the Company has a Whistleblower Policy for employees and non-employee stakeholders in India and 
all global locations. The employees are encouraged to report to the Whistleblower Administrator if they observe any fraudulent 
financial or other information or conduct that results in instances of unethical behaviour, or actual or suspected violations of the 
Company’s Code of Conduct and the Ethics Policy.
The employees are actively encouraged to reach out to the Whistleblower Administrator if they observe any fraudulent activity, 
questionable financial practices, or conduct that appears unethical, or if they suspect violations of the Company’s Code of 
Conduct or Ethics Policy. Beginning FY 2025-26, the Head of the Ethics Committee serves as the Whistleblower Administrator, 
personally overseeing the investigation process from the initial complaint through to its resolution. All findings and outcomes 
are subsequently reported to the Chairperson of the Audit Committee. Importantly, complainants are permitted to submit their 
concerns in any local language, ensuring accessibility for all.
The Company has also taken proactive initiatives to train employees and raise awareness about the Vigil Mechanism, reinforcing 
a culture of transparency and ethical conduct. These initiatives, along with the policy itself, provide robust safeguards to protect 
employees from any form of victimisation when they report issues to the Whistleblower Administrator.

Details of Non-compliance
During the year under review, an application for compounding of an offence under Section 96 of the Companies 
Act, 2013 was filed with the Regional Director, Mumbai in respect of M/s. Capiot Software Private Limited, a Wholly 
Owned subsidiary Company which was merged with your Company. The said violation pertained to non-compliance 
with the provisions relating to the holding of the Annual General Meeting within the prescribed timelines. The 
application was duly considered by the Regional Director, Mumbai, and the offence has been compounded upon 
payment of the requisite compounding fee as determined under the Act. The Company has taken note of the matter 
and has instituted necessary measures to further strengthen its compliance framework and ensure adherence to 
statutory timelines on a continual basis.
The aforesaid compounding does not have any material impact on the financial statements, operations, or other 
business activities of the Listed Company. The management continues to maintain robust compliance systems and 
periodic monitoring mechanisms to mitigate such instances going forward.
There were no non-compliances by the Company, no penalties and strictures were imposed on the Company by 
Stock Exchanges, SEBI or any statutory authority, on any matter related to the capital markets, during the year 
April 1, 2025, to March 31, 2026.
The Company has complied with and disclosed all the mandatory requirements under the Listing Regulations.
There are no qualifications or observations in the Secretarial Audit Report for FY 2025-26.

The Company constantly communicates to the institutional investors about the operations and financial results of 
the Company. Besides publishing the abridged financial results in one national and one regional daily newspaper, 
respectively, as per Regulation 46 of the Listing Regulations, the complete audited / limited reviewed financial

day as the release of results to the stock exchanges, through emails to all shareowners whose email IDs are registered

Are the premises / offices of the entity accessible to differently abled employees and workers, as per the 
requirements of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016? If not, whether any steps are being taken by 
the entity in this regard. 
Yes, Persistent Systems has a strong emphasis on accessibility and inclusion, with a focus on creating enablement 
friendly workplaces for persons with disabilities. The Company is committed to providing an inclusive, barrier free 
work environment and endeavours to ensure that its offices and premises are accessible in line with the Rights of 
Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016, and the Harmonised Guidelines issued thereunder.
	
Persistent offices are designed to accommodate the needs of persons with disabilities and include features such 
as accessible parking spaces, ramps at entry points, elevators, appropriate signage, disabled friendly restrooms, 
and height adjustable workstations, including provisions to support wheelchair users. Across all leased facilities, 
the Company ensures that accessibility requirements for persons with disabilities are duly addressed. In the digital 
environment, Persistent follows recognised accessibility standards and adheres to the Web Content Accessibility 
Guidelines (WCAG 2.0) to enhance accessibility of internal digital platforms. Where required, assistive 
technologies and reasonable accommodations are provided to support employees with specific needs. The 
Company conducts periodic reviews and audits of its facilities and undertakes necessary infrastructure upgrades 
on a continuous basis to further strengthen accessibility and inclusion, ensuring that individuals of all abilities can 
seamlessly access and engage with both physical and digital work environments. All our India Owned facilities 
including leased facilities are accessible to Persons with Disabilities.

effectiveness. Outcomes of these discussions are aligned with the Company’s broader ESG commitments and

Persistent Systems operates a mature, ISO/IEC 22301:2019–aligned Business Continuity Management System 
(BCMS) framework, integrated with ISO/IEC 27001 controls and embedded within Enterprise Risk Management. 
The framework spans all entities—subsidiaries, locations, functions and customer accounts—and is governed 
by defined roles with oversight from the Board’s Risk Management Committee and the CISO. BCM is driven 
by Business Impact Analysis and risk assessments, with resilience priorities aligned to financial materiality 
and contractual risk. Business Continuity Plans (BCPs) are implemented for critical services and key customer 
engagements, supported by industry-leading RTOs (up to 24 hours) and RPOs (up to 15 minutes). A multi-tiered 
approach, integrated with cyber resilience, crisis playbooks, and SOPs, ensures effective incident response. 
Robust Disaster Recovery (DR) testing, along with regular drills, simulations, and BC / DR exercises, is conducted 
to validate recovery capabilities and assure readiness. Periodic reviews and test outcomes drive continuous 
improvement and sustained operational resilience.

team, executes the CAPA plan. Implementation progress is monitored, reviewed periodically and updated within 
the PiQ system until completion.
	
Resolution confirmation and formal closure: Upon resolution, the Delivery Partner secures customer 
acknowledgement of closure. The SQA team validates the effectiveness of actions taken and formally closes the 
escalation in PiQ, with relevant internal stakeholders kept informed.

Global Business Outlook
The global economy enters Financial Year 2025-26 against a backdrop of slowing growth and renewed inflationary 
pressure. These conditions are linked to last year’s trade barriers and elevated uncertainty, with ongoing conflict in 
the Middle East compounding the strain. The challenges are particularly acute for emerging markets and developing 
economies, which remain more vulnerable to external shocks and financial instability.
While increased defense spending in response to geopolitical tension may provide a temporary boost to economic 
activity, it also intensifies inflationary pressure and strains fiscal health, raising the likelihood of social unrest in fragile 
regions. The overall outlook remains clouded by substantial downside risks, including prolonged conflict, deepening 
geopolitical fragmentation and the resurgence of protectionist trade policies.
In this volatile environment, organisations are under pressure to strike a careful balance between cost efficiency 
and the need to build resilience, agility and progress toward climate objectives, especially as regulatory frameworks 
grow more complex and unpredictable. At the same time, rapid advances in automation and artificial intelligence 
are helping to reduce operational workloads, but these technologies require strong governance structures and 
proactive workforce reskilling to ensure successful integration. As your Company looks to 2026 and 2027, the pace of 
disruption is accelerating, with technology companies moving from experimental AI pilots to large-scale, ROI-focused 
deployments that prioritise safety, security and regulatory compliance, while also laying the groundwork for the 
adoption of transformative quantum technologies.
Company Outlook
Your Company is a premier global provider of digital engineering and enterprise modernisation services. With more 
than 27,500 employees across 21 countries, it specialises in AI-driven solutions and software product engineering for 
industries such as BFSI, Healthcare and Hi-Tech, with deep expertise in building software products from conception 
to deployment. Its focus is on embedding AI-driven solutions across platforms, helping enterprises move from 
technical debt to competitive differentiation through a platform mindset.
Your company’s strategic approach centers on AI readiness through modern technology and data stacks, enabling 
clients to become value creators. It modernises core platforms and embeds AI across operations, aligning 
modernisation with strategic priorities to accelerate product launches, improve cost-to-income ratios and build 
customer trust. From product engineering to cloud and AI-powered automation, your Company drives smarter, safer 
and more sustainable industrial ecosystems. Its expertise in building next-generation software products at speed, with 
breakthrough operational efficiency, continues to be valued by its clients and its focus on delivering insights-driven, 
omnichannel customer experiences using best-in-class technologies underpins the long-term relationships it sustains 
with most of its customers.
Building the AI-led Enterprise 
For most enterprises, the question is no longer whether to adopt Generative AI, but where AI creates genuine value 
and where greater autonomy introduces risk. The market is shifting decisively from experimentation to disciplined, 
large-scale production. Generative AI is now firmly established from pilot to deployment, toward Agentic AI woven 
into core business processes. Yet realising AI’s full potential remains demanding. Integrating intelligence with  
existing enterprise systems is both complex and expensive and outcomes must be governed, secure and dependable 
at scale.
Your Company’s AI strategy is anchored on three reinforcing pillars, underpinned by Responsible AI. Engineering 
Hyper-Productivity embeds AI across the software development lifecycle, so engineering teams deliver faster, raise 
quality and do more with less. Business Hyper-Productivity applies AI to automate and optimise business process 
workflows and decision-making across enterprise functions, enabling organisations to drive efficiency and faster 
outcomes. Enterprise Data Readiness prepares the enterprise data foundation, with the right structure, governance 
and accessibility so AI can deliver accurate, contextual and trusted outcomes at scale. Together, these pillars define 
the path enterprises must take to realise the full value of AI. Success lies in the last mile, making AI-driven outcomes 
repeatable, transparent and governed at scale, so that the desired business outcome is sustained and trusted across 
the enterprise.

INR/$ Currency Movement
The Company minimises the foreign currency fluctuation risk as per the Company’s Foreign Exchange Risk 
Management Policy. The Company holds plain vanilla forward contracts against a portion of expected future 
receivables in USD to manage the risk of changes in exchange rates.
As per the accounting principles laid down in Ind AS 109 – ‘Financial Instruments’ relating to cash flow hedges, 
derivative financial instruments which qualify for cash flow hedge accounting are fair valued at balance sheet 
date and the effective portion of the resultant loss / (gain) is debited / (credited) to the hedge reserve under other 
comprehensive income and  
the ineffective portion is recognised in the statement of profit and loss. Derivative financial instruments are carried 
as forward contract receivable when the fair value is positive and as forward contract payable when the fair value is 
negative.
Changes in the fair value of derivative instruments that do not qualify for hedge accounting are recognised in the 
statement of profit and loss as they arise. Hedge accounting is discontinued when the hedging instrument expires 
or is sold, or terminated, or exercised or no longer qualifies for hedge accounting. Any cumulative gain or loss on the 
hedging instrument recognised under other comprehensive income is transferred to the statement of profit and loss 
when the forecasted transaction occurs or affects profit or loss or when a hedged transaction is no longer expected to 
occur.
Accordingly, the Forward Cover Reserve (net of tax effects) as at March 31, 2026, stood at a debit balance of INR 
1,676.01 Million as against a debit balance of INR 2.32 Million as at March 31, 2025. Please refer to ‘Other Equity’ 
under Statement of Changes in Equity in the consolidated financials for details.

While consolidating the financial statements of subsidiaries (including step down subsidiaries) with the financial 
statements of the Parent Company, the assets and liabilities are stated in Indian Rupees by applying the closing 
exchange rates, equity is stated in Indian Rupees by applying the historical exchange rates and income and 
expenditure are stated in Indian Rupees by applying the average exchange rates. This creates an exchange difference 
on consolidation, which is accumulated under the foreign currency translation reserve.
